correctness.rationale: The exact net-crossing transition rule makes the incoming parent edge have reverse weight exp(-beta), while the b_i child edges and two private-cycle edges are unused and weight one. Conditional outward probability is b_0/(b_0+2) at the root and b_i/(b_i+2+exp(-beta)) at later levels; multiplying exact finite cylinder events then taking a decreasing limit proves the product. Bounds x/(1+x)<=log(1+x)<=x imply positivity iff sum 1/b_i converges. Along the event graph distance to the root diverges, and the explicit exponential branching lower bound follows by direct summation. The independently constructed truncated graphs reproduce the transitions in 10942 rational comparisons; the analytic argument, not computation, proves the infinite statement.

value.rationale: The primary source specifically asks whether an infinite leaf is necessary to avoid directed-circuit trapping, and only informally sketches a graph with growing cycles. The result gives an explicit proof of positive escape even when every vertex lies on a cycle of fixed length, with a sharp exact criterion controlling the natural strictly-outward event and a beta-uniform positive lower bound. It identifies branching rather than cycle-length growth as the sufficient structural mechanism and leaves the broader dichotomy untouched.
